entries.name: Ableton AI
entries.author: Freek Van der Herten and contributors
entries.description: A small pattern can become a whole mood. Make a loop, play with its pulse, and keep the happy accidents.
entries.tagline: Control Ableton Live from an AI assistant via MCP

entries.name: Autonomous Circuit
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Describe a board; get a fab-ready PCB with a live board view, ordered from JLCPCB in a click.
entries.tagline: Get a verified PCB and a fab packet you can order

examples.prompt: Design a six-key USB macropad. Start with the schematic.
examples.caption: Six-key USB-C macropad · RP2040, 43 parts, 84×47 mm · fab-ready for JLCPCB

examples.prompt: Design a USB-C desk weather badge: an RP2040 reads a BME280 temperature, humidity and pressure sensor and shows comfort on a bar of five RGB LEDs, with one button to cycle modes.
examples.caption: USB-C weather badge · RP2040 + BME280 + 5 RGB LEDs, 55 parts, 80×64 mm · fab-ready for JLCPCB

entries.name: Grid
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Talk to your fleet. Deploy open-weight models, find the right machine for each workload, and watch your Grid come alive with a live map of engines, models, memory, temperature and performance.
entries.tagline: Deploy open-weight models across your machines and watch the fleet live

entries.name: Autonomous Workshop
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Describe a part; get a validated, printable STEP with a live 3D view.
entries.tagline: AI inventors that make new toys and games

examples.prompt: Design a cable clip that holds three 6 mm cables to the edge of a 20 mm thick desk, printable without supports.
examples.caption: Three-cable desk clip · one support-free PETG part · verified STEP, 38 × 33 × 14 mm

examples.prompt: Design a honeycomb desk organizer: seven hexagonal cups for pens, brushes and scissors, stepping up in height around a tall centre cup, printable in one piece without supports.
examples.caption: Honeycomb desk organizer · 7 hex cups, one support-free print · verified STEP, 89 × 92 × 104 mm

entries.name: autoresearch-mlx
entries.author: Trevin creator; Andrej Karpathy
entries.description: Follow a small idea through a real experiment. Train, compare, and see what the evidence says.
entries.tagline: Karpathy's autoresearch on Apple Silicon, no PyTorch required

entries.name: Blender
entries.author: Blender Foundation
entries.description: Describe an object, a scene, a shot — and watch it take shape: modelled in Blender's Python, rendered headless, exported as glTF you can orbit and zoom in the pane.
entries.tagline: Free and open source 3D creation software

examples.prompt: Make a cozy isometric reading nook: a cut-away corner of a room with an armchair, a floor lamp glowing warm, a bookshelf full of colourful books, a round rug and a monstera, with evening sun through the window and a cat asleep on the rug.
examples.caption: Isometric reading nook · 122 named objects, 35 materials · glTF + Cycles render

examples.prompt: Model a small desk robot toy: a rounded body, a head with two round eyes, two arms that rotate at the shoulders, an antenna, and a round base. Separate named objects in collections, real sizes in millimetres, and nice materials.
examples.caption: Desk robot toy · 29 named parts, 10 materials · glTF + Cycles render

entries.name: Bonsai MCP
entries.author: Show2Instruct
entries.description: Make room for a new idea. Shape a small building, inspect its spaces, and open the real IFC model anywhere.
entries.tagline: MCP server for a live Blender + Bonsai (BlenderBIM) session

entries.name: CAD Viewer
entries.author: Jake Fitzgerald
entries.description: Jake Fitzgerald's CAD Viewer (earthtojake/text-to-cad) as a Harness pane: STEP, GLB, STL, 3MF, DXF, URDF, SRDF and SDF, with MoveIt2 inverse kinematics.

entries.name: CircuitJS
entries.author: Paul Falstad
entries.description: Describe a circuit — an RC filter, a 555 flasher, an amplifier — and watch it run in the pane: charge animating along the wires, scope traces drawing, every value still yours to poke at.
entries.tagline: Electronic circuit simulator in the browser

examples.prompt: Build a two-transistor flasher that alternates three red and three blue LEDs like a police light, about twice a second, with a scope on each side and a knob for each side's on-time.
examples.caption: Police-light flasher · two-transistor astable, ~2.2 Hz · 2 scopes + 2 timing knobs

examples.prompt: Build a 555 astable LED flasher with a potentiometer that sets the rate, and scopes on the capacitor and the output.
examples.caption: 555 LED flasher · running live, ~1.1 Hz · rate knob + 2 scopes

entries.name: Comfy MCP
entries.author: Comfy Org
entries.description: Follow a visual thread. Explore a family of forms, collect your favourites, and keep the recipe with every image.
entries.tagline: Local MCP server for ComfyUI — run ComfyUI from AI agents

entries.name: Creative Direction
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Build a coherent visual identity with coordinated posters, typography and palettes. Compare art directions, lock colors, customize a name, and export SVG posters and design tokens.
entries.tagline: Build a coherent visual identity with coordinated posters, typography and palett

examples.prompt: Create a coastal identity for COVE STUDIO: mineral green, warm paper, an expressive serif, and a poster that feels like a place to stay.
examples.caption: Forme · interactive offline starter

entries.name: DimOS
entries.author: Dimensional
entries.description: Send a little rover on a small adventure. Pick a destination, watch it find a way, and replay the journey.
entries.tagline: The agentic operating system for physical space

entries.name: Doc Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A reader for the PDF a harness is writing: thumbnails, the outline, find, zoom and two-page spreads on pdf.js — redrawn in place on every compile, changed pages marked, compile errors shown over the last good pages.

entries.name: Drone Pilot
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Fly a seeded canyon course in first person. Switch between manual controls and a tracking autopilot, inspect gate results and the flight path, and export telemetry.
entries.tagline: Fly a seeded canyon course in first person

examples.prompt: Design a slalom course over a canyon floor. Make the autopilot fly a clean lap, then give me manual controls and a trace to compare against it.
examples.caption: Vector · interactive offline starter

entries.name: Excalidraw
entries.author: Excalidraw
entries.description: Describe a diagram — an architecture, a flow, a whiteboard sketch — and watch it appear hand-drawn in the pane, as an .excalidraw file you can open anywhere.
entries.tagline: Collaborative whiteboarding made easy

examples.prompt: Map an online store's checkout as a flowchart: cart, sign-in or guest checkout, shipping, payment with a declined-card retry loop, a fraud check that can send orders to manual review, then order confirmed and the email receipt. Diamonds for decisions, one frame per stage.
examples.caption: Checkout flowchart · 3 decisions, retry loop, 3 frames · .excalidraw

examples.prompt: Draw the architecture of a URL shortener: browser, CDN, API service, Postgres, Redis cache, a click-tracking worker on a queue, and an analytics dashboard. Frame the backend and label the arrows.
examples.caption: URL shortener architecture · 10 shapes, 8 labeled arrows · .excalidraw

entries.name: Film Viewer
entries.author: OpenHarness contributors
entries.description: A screening room for OpenMontage productions: live storyboards, a film player, render versions, and notes tied to a moment in the cut.

entries.name: Foam-Agent
entries.author: Foam-Agent team
entries.description: Give the wind something to move around. Explore shapes, trace the currents, and compare your experiments.
entries.tagline: Composable multi-agent framework for CFD simulations in OpenFOAM

entries.name: Game Master
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Design and compare strategies in a seeded arena. Watch two squads compete for relays, inspect decisions, step and rewind matches, and run a 32-map tournament.
entries.tagline: Design and compare strategies in a seeded arena

examples.prompt: Create a capture arena where patient defenders face aggressive hunters. Show every decision and compare their win rates over 32 maps.
examples.caption: Relay · interactive offline starter

entries.name: Game Viewer
entries.author: OpenHarness contributors
entries.description: A live game studio: playable previews, real build progress, versions, and an uninterrupted last working game while the next one takes shape.

entries.name: Generative Art
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Design reproducible generative editions. Explore contour fields, dunes and orbital studies, tune their geometry and palettes, and export prints up to 3200 × 4000.
entries.tagline: Design reproducible generative editions

examples.prompt: Create an edition of 12 tidal contour prints in indigo and burnt orange. Keep the paper quiet and make each seed feel related but distinct.
examples.caption: Fieldwork · interactive offline starter

entries.name: Godogen
entries.author: Alex Ermolov
entries.description: Build a world you can play. Watch your game take shape in a live studio, explore each version, and play while the agent keeps creating.
entries.tagline: Autonomous game development

examples.prompt: Make a synthwave hoverbike racer: ride down a neon grid canyon toward a striped setting sun, weave between glowing pylons, hop barriers and collect energy cores, with a boost and three shields.
examples.caption: Neon Drift · 3D synthwave hoverbike racer · playable in Game Studio

examples.prompt: Make a low-poly sailing game: steer a little sloop around a sunny archipelago of palm islands with a lighthouse, find twelve floating treasure chests marked by beams of light before the sun sets, and watch out for reefs.
examples.caption: Treasure Isles · 3D low-poly sailing treasure hunt · playable in Game Studio

entries.name: Jev Archer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live archery range. Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the archer, tracking a target sliding across a line. Every tick Jev reads the target and the aim point and nudges the aim to track it, releasing an arrow each window. Speed the target up and Jev's aim trails and misses pile up.
entries.tagline: Jev takes aim at a sliding target, planting every arrow in the bullseye, live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Archer up for a hard range — speed the target up so it slides faster than Jev's aim can correct. Give Jev a lead-the-motion aiming style, then watch it read the target every tick, nudge the aim to track, and release arrow after arrow into (or past) the bullseye.
examples.caption: Jev's Day on the Range — a fast decision model tracking the sliding target and planting the bullseye on each shot

entries.name: Jev Arena
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live grid world powered by Jev, TypeSafe's System One model. Jev decides every move in real time — watch its probability distributions and confidence as it thinks, and redesign the world to test it.
entries.tagline: Watch a decision model think

examples.prompt: Redesign the arena into the Vault Heist: Jev starts outside the bank, must slip between the walls to the vault star, and grab the three gold bars (coins) on the way while avoiding the security lasers (walls). Make it a tight maze that forces a few sharp turns so Jev's confidence dips and recovers.
examples.caption: The Vault Heist · a tight maze where Jev's probability bars visibly shift at each turn

entries.name: Jev Blocks
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A falling-blocks puzzle played live by Jev, TypeSafe's System One model. One call per piece picks a placement from every legal one, with a probability for each, drawn on the board. The piece keeps falling while Jev thinks. Raise gravity and find where it breaks. A synthetic demo.
entries.tagline: Jev plays a falling-blocks puzzle, its whole mind drawn on the board, live

examples.prompt: Design a hard challenge for Jev Blocks: start with 6 garbage rows, use an S and Z heavy piece mix, set gravity to 12 with a speedup of 1, and write a style line that tells Jev to dig out first. Then watch the pane and tell me at what gravity Jev starts to miss placements.
examples.caption: Find the breaking point: a fast decision model placing every piece while it really falls

examples.prompt: Draw a custom starting board in blocks.json that is one I piece away from clearing four lines, keep gravity low, and tell Jev to go for four. Report whether it takes the four-line clear.
examples.caption: A hand-drawn board to test whether Jev sees the four-line clear

entries.name: Jev Browser
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Jev operates a web browser, live. On a made-up travel site it books flights in seconds: each step the page is written out as text and Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, picks one element from the list. Add pop-ups and layout shifts, or click the page yourself, and watch it cope.
entries.tagline: Jev drives a web browser: a flight booked in seconds, one pick per step

examples.prompt: Write ten booking tasks for a family trip: different cities, days and bag counts, some nonstop only. Then raise distraction until fewer than 9 in 10 bookings come out exactly right, and tell me where that is.
examples.caption: A flight booked exactly as asked in 1.5 seconds and 10 steps, checked against the task

examples.prompt: Slow it down to one step a second with no distraction so I can read what Jev sees and what it picks at every step.
examples.caption: Step mode: the page text Jev reads on the right, its chosen element ringed on the page

entries.name: Jev Catcher
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live fielding demo. Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the outfielder, guarding the line as pop flies drop to random spots. Every tick Jev reads the glove's position and the next ball's landing spot and slides to catch it. Speed the falls up and Jev's glove can't keep up and the drops pile up.
entries.tagline: Jev guards the outfield, sliding to catch each pop fly as it falls, live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Catcher up for a hard session — speed the pop flies up so they drop faster than Jev can chase. Give Jev a burst-to-the-spot fielding style, then watch it read the landing spot every tick, slide the glove across the grass, and catch (or drop) each ball as it falls.
examples.caption: Jev's Day at the Field — a fast decision model sliding the glove to catch every pop fly on each tick

entries.name: Jev Compactor
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live demo of instant context compaction on a made-up coding-agent session. When the window passes its budget, Jev judges every tool result in one pass: keep, trim or drop. Recall is measured against hidden ground truth. Raise distraction and Jev keeps junk and loses needles.
entries.tagline: Watch Jev compact a made-up agent session in one pass, measured honestly

examples.prompt: Design a session for a made-up repo: five tasks with sharp, separate vocabularies, a 300,000 token budget and trimTo 300. Then find the highest distraction where needle recall still stays above 90% while the reduction stays above 70%. Report the numbers you saw.
examples.caption: A synthetic agent session where Jev judges every tool result at once and the context tower collapses

entries.name: Jev Conductor
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the composer. It improvises a live piece bar by bar: chords, bass and melody in real time, played through the Web Audio API. Edit moods, tempo, scales and chords while it's playing and the music changes.
entries.tagline: Jev improvises a live tune you watch being written

examples.prompt: Jev is improvising a warm, nocturnal jazz tune. Set a slow tempo, lush 7th chords, and a brooding-to-hopeful mood arc. Live up to the name.
examples.caption: Jev in Blue — a slow, moody jazz improvisation

entries.name: Jev Duel
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live Reversi battle where Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — plays BOTH sides and a third Jev referees. Two rivals with distinct personalities fight for the board, the referee calls every move, and you can edit the rivals mid-game.
entries.tagline: Jev plays both sides of a Reversi war, and a third Jev referees

examples.prompt: Stage a grudge match: a patient corner-lover called Patience against a greedy opportunist called Greed. Make their personalities clash and watch the referee call it as the game tips.
examples.caption: The Quiet War — patience vs greed on a 6x6 board

entries.name: Jev Firehose
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live map-reduce demo on made-up data. Thousands of synthetic inbox messages stream in, and Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, triages each one in a single call with five parallel questions. Unsure ones go to an escalate lane. Speed, cost, count and measured accuracy climb as you watch.
entries.tagline: Jev triages thousands of made-up inbox messages live: fast, cheap, measured

examples.prompt: Turn the desk into player support for a made-up game studio. Write 8 teams with sharp descriptions and at least 6 phrases each. Then find the lowest threshold that keeps auto-routing above 95% right at noise 0.3, and tell me how many messages it escalates.
examples.caption: A new desk designed by the agent, with a measured threshold

examples.prompt: Make it hard. Set noise to 0.7 and tell me what happens to accuracy and escalations, which two teams get mixed up most, and which threshold you would pick.
examples.caption: Turn the noise dial and read the trade-off on synthetic data

entries.name: Jev FPS
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Jev plays a first-person arena shooter, live. About nine times a second the fight is written out as text and Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, answers four typed questions in one call: turn, move, fire and threat. Redraw the map, speed up the demons, or grab the controls yourself.
entries.tagline: Jev plays a first-person shooter live: turn, move and fire, nine times a second

examples.prompt: Build me a tight maze level with a boss room in the middle and three demon spawns in the corners. Start the demons slow, then find the demon speed where Jev stops clearing wave 3.
examples.caption: Jev fights through a hand-drawn ASCII map while its keys light up with each decision's probability

examples.prompt: Make it brutal: 8 demons at once, fast, in one big open room with no cover. Tell Jev to keep its back to a wall. How many waves does it survive?
examples.caption: A stress test for a decision model: more demons, more speed, the same nine decisions a second

entries.name: Jev Guard
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is your code reviewer. You fix a tiny broken module and Jev's guard judges every edit live: how close to the goal, how risky, how much it trusts it. Watch a decision model referee your own coding as you work.
entries.tagline: Jev referees your own coding, edit by edit

examples.prompt: Fix the broken module in project/ so every test in test.js passes. Make Jev Guard watch you work and tell you — live — when your change is risky and when the goal is truly met.
examples.caption: Ship it green — Jev guarding your fix, run by run

entries.name: Jev Lander
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live landing demo. A booster falls out of the sky under gravity; Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the flight computer, reading altitude, vertical speed and fuel every tick and setting a throttle to bring it down soft. Crank the gravity up and watch the touchdowns start to crash.
entries.tagline: Jev is the flight computer, bringing a booster down soft, live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Lander up as a rough descent — boost the gravity and cut the fuel. Give Jev a decisive burn-early style line, then watch it read the telemetry every tick, throttle the booster down the pad, and land soft (or slam in when gravity is too high and the burns go twitchy).
examples.caption: Jev's Landing — a fast decision model flying a booster down to a soft touchdown on every tick

entries.name: Jev Launcher
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live predictive command palette. As you type, Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — re-ranks your launch targets on every keystroke, showing which one it would fire and how confident it is. Curate the palette; Jev does the ranking.
entries.tagline: Jev ranks a command palette live as you type

examples.prompt: Set Jev Launcher up as a developer's command palette — targets for run-tests, open-editor, deploy, chat, music — each with good aliases. Type partial queries and watch Jev re-rank the field on every keystroke, then fire the winner on paper.
examples.caption: Jev's Palette — a fast decision model ranking launch targets live, per keystroke

entries.name: Jev Pendulum
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live inverted-pendulum experiment. A stiff rod stands upright on a pivot; Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — chooses a corrective torque every tick to keep it from toppling. Turn gravity up and watch Jev start to lose it; the balance is the show.
entries.tagline: Jev balances an inverted pendulum live on a pivot

examples.prompt: Set Jev Pendulum up as a tense balancing rig — a stiff rod under gravity 8 with a gust every few ticks that shoves it toward the fall line. Give Jev a style line for how to recover, then watch it hold, wobble, and eventually drop.
examples.caption: Jev's Balancing Act — a fast decision model keeping a rod upright, and losing it at high gravity

entries.name: Jev Pong
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live paddle-defense rally. Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the paddle: every tick it reads the ball and moves to meet the return. The ball speeds up with every hit, so a long rally is a losing battle — watch Jev chase, wobble, and finally drop it.
entries.tagline: Jev is the paddle — a rally that speeds up and outruns it

examples.prompt: Set Jev Pong up as a tense rally — a mid-size court at speed 6 with a gentle accel so the ball builds up over a few returns. Give Jev a decisive style line, then watch it hold the streak until the rally outruns the paddle.
examples.caption: Jev's Rally — a fast decision model chasing a ball that speeds up with every return

entries.name: Jev Sheets
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live spreadsheet where a column header is a question. Type "Urgent?" and Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, answers it for every row: one call per row, all columns at once, each cell shaded by confidence and flagged for review when unsure. Made-up data. Runs offline on a mock.
entries.tagline: Type a question as a column header and Jev answers it for every row, live

examples.prompt: Build me a sheet of 80 made-up job applications for a junior designer role. Add Jev columns: "Has a portfolio link?", "Fit: weak < fair < strong" and "Next step: reject = no relevant work | phone screen = some relevant work | interview = strong relevant work". Put in 15 rows with mixed signals, label the truth, then read the accuracy and sharpen the weakest question.
examples.caption: A header is a question: Jev fills every row in about a second, and the pane shows where it is unsure

examples.prompt: Turn the inbox sheet into a churn watch. Keep the rows, replace the columns with "Wants to cancel?", "Churn risk: low < medium < high" and "Reason: price | bugs | missing feature | support" with a clear meaning for each option. Then tell me which rows Jev is least sure about and why.
examples.caption: Reword the questions, watch only the changed column fill again, and review the low confidence cells

entries.name: Jev Shopper
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live price-watching demo. A small shop window streams prices; Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — reads the stream each tick and calls the best buy, showing how sure it is and spending on paper when the signal is strong. Turn up the volatility and watch Jev's calls start to flip.
entries.tagline: Jev calls the best buy as a shop's prices stream in, live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Shopper up as a weekend-camp haul — a few pieces of gear with divergent price drifts. Give Jev a decisive momentum style line, then watch it read the window each tick, call the steepest faller, and commit the paper budget when the signal is clear. Crank the volatility to see its calls start to flip.
examples.caption: Jev's Shop — a fast decision model calling the best buy on every live price tick

entries.name: Jev Slalom
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A live skiing demo. Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — is the racer, carving a slalom line as the gates sweep toward it, steering left and right to thread each gap. Crank the descent speed up and Jev's aim starts to wobble and it clips a gate and falls.
entries.tagline: Jev skis the slalom, threading each gate as it sweeps by, live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Slalom up as a hard run — push the descent speed up near the limit. Give Jev a decisive line-up-early style, then watch it read the next gate every tick, carve the valley, thread every gate (or clip one and fall when the speed gets too hot).
examples.caption: Jev's Run — a fast decision model carving a slalom line and threading each gate on every tick

entries.name: Jev Trader
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — runs a paper-trading desk on a synthetic market. It reads the price tape and its own P&L, then decides buy, hold or sell, tick by tick. Watch the equity curve move as a decision model trades. Reshape instrument, volatility and style while it runs.
entries.tagline: Jev runs a paper-trading desk you can watch trade live

examples.prompt: Set Jev Trader as a momentum desk on a volatile synthetic instrument — high volatility, a trend-following style. Watch whether it buys the upswings and cuts the downswings, and keep it honest on paper.
examples.caption: Jev's Desk — a decision model trading a synthetic market, tick by tick

entries.name: JUCE Agent Toolkit
entries.author: Daniel Raffel
entries.description: Find a sound that feels like you. Shape a synth, play a little, and take the recording with you.
entries.tagline: JUCE workflow skills for Codex, Cursor, Claude Code and other agent CLIs

entries.name: KiCad
entries.author: KiCad
entries.description: Describe a board; get a real KiCad project — a wired schematic, DRC-checked copper, a prototype packet — with a live board view.
entries.tagline: A real KiCad project: wired schematic, DRC-checked copper, a prototype packet

entries.name: Lab Bench
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Explore an experiment with reproducible synthetic data. Change effect, noise and sample size, probe observations, filter groups, inspect computed uncertainty, and export CSV.
entries.tagline: Explore an experiment with reproducible synthetic data

examples.prompt: Build a synthetic catalyst experiment. Let me vary the true effect and noise, compare groups, inspect uncertainty, and export the observations.
examples.caption: Signal · interactive offline starter

entries.name: Manim
entries.author: Manim Community
entries.description: Describe an explanation — a proof, a transform, an algorithm, a graph — and watch it animate: scenes in Python, rendered by Manim, playing in the pane.
entries.tagline: Python library for creating mathematical animations

examples.prompt: Draw a chess knight using nothing but spinning circles: a Fourier series of 120 epicycles, tip to tail, tracing its silhouette in gold.
examples.caption: Fourier knight · 120 epicycles · 17 s 1080p60 MP4, 4 chapters

examples.prompt: Animate the Pythagorean theorem in about 20 seconds: draw a 3-4-5 right triangle, grow squares on its three sides with their areas labelled, then show 9 + 16 = 25.
examples.caption: Pythagorean theorem · 20 s animation · 1080p MP4

entries.name: marimo
entries.author: marimo
entries.description: Describe an analysis, a model, a dashboard — and watch the reactive notebook come alive in the pane: marimo's own editor on the notebook the agent writes, cells re-running as it types.
entries.tagline: Next-generation Python notebook

examples.prompt: Build a notebook that explores the Lorenz attractor: sliders for σ, ρ and β, the butterfly drawn in two projections coloured by time, and two runs started a hair apart to show how fast they diverge.
examples.caption: Lorenz butterfly explorer · σ/ρ/β sliders, chaos stats, two projections

examples.prompt: Build a notebook that simulates a coffee shop queue over a day, with a slider for the arrival rate and the number of baristas, and a chart of wait times through the day.
examples.caption: Coffee-queue simulator · reactive sliders, KPI cards, wait-time chart

entries.name: Marp
entries.author: Yuki Hattori
entries.description: Describe a talk; get a keynote — huge type, generated art, speaker notes — live in the pane, exported to PDF, PPTX or HTML.
entries.tagline: Create beautiful slide decks using Markdown

examples.prompt: Make a ten-minute keynote for a science festival about the deep ocean: how deep it goes, how little of the seafloor we have mapped, and the global push to finish the map by 2030.
examples.caption: Deep-sea keynote · 9 slides, ocean art, seafloor chart, speaker notes

examples.prompt: Make a keynote for the internal launch of Harness, a Mac app that runs coding agents in persistent terminals you can reach from any device, with a live viewer for the work they produce. Audience: 200 engineers at an all-hands. 10 minutes. Include a chart with our growth: 12 teams in 2023, 31 in 2024, 64 in 2025, 140 today.
examples.caption: Launch keynote · 10 slides, generated art, growth chart, speaker notes

entries.name: 3D Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A Blender-style viewport for the glTF a harness exports — outliner, properties in mm, shading modes, measure, section, explode, scene camera, timeline — live on every export.

entries.name: MuJoCo
entries.author: Google DeepMind
entries.description: Describe a robot, a scene, a controller — a Unitree quadruped standing, a humanoid learning to walk — and watch the rollout play: MuJoCo physics, Menagerie robots, MJX for training.
entries.tagline: Advanced physics simulation

examples.prompt: Make the Unitree G1 humanoid say hello: stand, raise its right hand and wave three times, then lower it and take a small bow. Record it.
examples.caption: Unitree G1 humanoid · wave hello + bow · 29 servos, 11 s rollout, live in the MuJoCo Viewer

examples.prompt: Load the Unitree Go2, make it stand, then do three slow squats and wave the front left leg. Record it.
examples.caption: Unitree Go2 · 3 squats + a wave · 21 s rollout, live in the MuJoCo Viewer

entries.name: MuJoCo Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: MuJoCo's own simulate, in the pane: live physics you can push, pull and pause, every actuator on a slider, contacts and forces drawn, sensors plotted, and the agent's recording replayed frame by frame — on MuJoCo's WebAssembly build.

entries.name: Music Studio
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Compose a seeded eight-bar track, edit five instrument patterns, shape swing and the mix, listen locally, and export the result as a WAV file.
entries.tagline: Compose a seeded eight-bar track, edit five instrument patterns, shape swing and

entries.name: OpenMontage

examples.prompt: Make a 12-second title sequence for a riverside night market called Lanterns: paper lanterns drifting up over dark water with their reflections trembling, then the title and dates glowing in. Three shots, warm and hand-made, no stock footage.

entries.name: Phaser

entries.description: Describe a game — a breakout, a platformer, a shooter, a puzzle — and play it in the pane as the agent writes it in Phaser 4, reloading on every save.

entries.name: RDKit
entries.author: RDKit
entries.description: Describe a molecule — a drug, an analogue, a scaffold — and get it designed, its properties computed and a 3D conformer you can rotate in the pane.

examples.prompt: Take capsaicin, the molecule behind chili heat, and design three analogues: a saturated tail (nonivamide), a shorter tail, and the ester capsiate. Give each a 3D conformer and compare their properties side by side.

examples.prompt: Design three analogues of ibuprofen that keep the propionic acid but replace the isobutyl group with alternatives that lower cLogP below 3 while staying Lipinski-compliant. For each: SMILES, properties, a 3D conformer and a similarity score to ibuprofen. Pick the best one and explain the choice.
examples.caption: Ibuprofen + 3 lower-cLogP analogues · 3D conformers · ESP surface + series table

entries.name: Yosys
entries.author: YosysHQ
entries.description: Describe a digital circuit — a counter, a UART, a state machine — and get Verilog, a simulation with waveforms, a synthesized gate-level schematic and an FPGA bitstream for an iCE40 board. Prompt to silicon.
entries.tagline: Framework for Verilog RTL synthesis

examples.prompt: Build a tiny 8-bit CPU for the iCEBreaker that runs a Fibonacci program from ROM and prints every number over the USB serial port at 115200 baud; the button runs it again. Simulate it, check the serial output in the testbench and build the bitstream.
examples.caption: Tiny 8-bit CPU printing Fibonacci over UART · 8 checks pass · 294 LCs, 26.1 MHz · iCE40 bitstream

examples.prompt: Design a UART transmitter at 115200 baud from the 12 MHz clock that sends the text HELLO followed by newline each time the button is pressed (debounced), plus a breathing PWM on the green LED. Testbench must decode the serial frames and check the bytes. Run the whole flow, keep Fmax above 12 MHz, and report LUTs and Fmax.
examples.caption: HELLO over UART + breathing LED · 25 checks pass · 226 LCs, 51.9 MHz · iCE40 bitstream
